rows.ackNote: Automatic acknowledgement: passed for handling, applications taken in order of receipt
rows.outcome: *** ANSWERED, AND IT IS A YES. *** IU.631.434.2026, dated 22 September 2026, signed by the Director KAROLINA KAWCZYŃSKA, case officer dr MAŁGORZATA URBANOWSKA-CHYŁA. The reply says the digital copies of the BIRTH, MARRIAGE AND DEATH registers of URZĄD STANU CYWILNEGO SZUBIN MIASTO “have already been made available some time ago” on www.genealogiawarchiwach.pl, and supplies a direct link to THE BIRTH REGISTER FOR 1884 — the year Jacob Leibholz was born at Schubin on 8 August. It explains how to expand the table of contents on the black bar to the left, and says the scan of any record found may be downloaded straight from the portal. NO FEE, NO QUERY SERVICE, NO ACKNOWLEDGEMENT REQUESTED — unlike the Koszalin reply, this one asks for nothing back. THE CONTRAST WITH KOSZALIN IS THE WHOLE POINT: the Hammerstein registers are gone and the Szubin ones were online the entire time this archive was writing letters about them.
rows.acknowledged: Not required — the letter asks for no confirmation of receipt.

rows.what: Czarne (Hammerstein) civil registers 1847 and 1884, and the synagogue books — the Leibholz family
rows.outcome: ANSWERED IN FIVE LINES AND IT IS A NEGATIVE. O-S.6342.406.2026, signed by Krzysztof Skrzypiec, Head of the Slupsk Branch. The Koszalin holdings contain NO registers of the former German civil registry office at Czarne (Standesamt Hammerstein, Kreis Schlochau) FOR 1874 TO 1899, and NO synagogue-community books for Czarne AT ALL — and no information about what became of either, or where they might now be held. *** ACKNOWLEDGED 17 SEPTEMBER, message 1a0ac71a500bc77f, in their own thread 1a0a98796538c64b, to slupsk@ as they asked and copied to the case officer. The acknowledgement tells them WHY a negative was useful — that it closes the only route to Georg Leibholz’s parents — thanks them specifically for saying they do not know where the books went, and closes the correspondence so they need not spend more time on it.

rows.ackNote: ANSWERED, and it is an invitation to apply. Mr Keyster: "Please, apply for copies. Application form is attached. Please, submit proof of payment and the application on groundfloor." Two things his reply does not give: whether an applicant in Australia may submit by email rather than in person, and the fee and banking details. Both have to be asked. REPLIED 15 September asking the two things his message left out: whether an applicant in Australia may submit by email rather than in person, and the fee and banking details for the required proof of payment. The reply also states plainly, in advance, that David is not a relative and makes no claim on either estate — so that a standing objection comes before the fee rather than after it.

The parish marriage register of 7 September 1940
rows.outcome: ANSWERED IN A WEEK, COURTEOUSLY, WITH THE WRONG BOOK — AND THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HAD IT. They sent the ORIGINAL MARRIAGE REGISTER, the Union civil form B.M.D. 3, entry no. 13 of 1940, which the priest completed as marriage officer. *** THAT FORM HAS NO PARENTS' COLUMNS, WHICH IS THE ONLY THING THE LETTER WANTED — and every field on it has been published here since 17 September, reconstructed from FamilySearch film 008161359 frame 475. *** WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW IS THAT THE PARISH ANSWERS: row 26 had been blocked on them since 15 September, and the books that do name parents are still in their building. A clean image also now exists and is published, where before the archive had only a table of fields. A SECOND LETTER IS OWED naming the LIBER MATRIMONIORUM and the BANNS REGISTER explicitly, because the distinction between the parish's own books and the state form it fills in is not obvious from outside.
